data.title: Regimens for atypical (non-tuberculous) mycobacterial infections
data.summary: Antituberculous drugs · Treatment of cutaneous infections by non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antituberculous drugs_

**Class:** Treatment of cutaneous infections by non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM)

## Mechanism of action
- NTM are naturally resistant to many first-line TB drugs; therapy is based on species and, for rapid growers, on sensitivity testing

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- M. marinum (fish tank/swimming pool granuloma): clarithromycin + ethambutol (or rifampicin), or minocycline/doxycycline or co-trimoxazole alone for limited disease — continue 1–2 months after lesions resolve (usually 3–4 months total)
- Rapid growers (M. fortuitum, M. chelonae, M. abscessus — post-injection/post-procedure abscesses): clarithromycin plus another drug by sensitivity (amikacin, ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin, linezolid, cefoxitin, imipenem) for 4–6 months; surgical debridement
- M. ulcerans (Buruli ulcer): rifampicin + clarithromycin for 8 weeks (WHO), surgery/grafting as needed
- M. avium complex: clarithromycin/azithromycin + ethambutol + rifampicin
- M. kansasii: rifampicin + ethambutol + isoniazid/macrolide

## Dose & formulations
- Clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily; ethambutol 15 mg/kg/day; rifampicin 10 mg/kg/day; minocycline/doxycycline 100 mg twice daily; co-trimoxazole 160/800 mg twice daily

## Adverse effects
- See component drugs; long courses need monitoring of liver, blood counts, vision (ethambutol), hearing (amikacin)

## Contraindications
- See component drugs

## Monitoring
- Culture and sensitivity for rapid growers; clinical response; drug toxicity monitoring

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid tetracyclines and aminoglycosides; macrolides with care.

## Viva points
- M. marinum — sporotrichoid spread on the hand; clarithromycin + ethambutol
- Rapid growers after injections/cosmetic procedures — clarithromycin-based combination by sensitivity
- Buruli ulcer — rifampicin + clarithromycin 8 weeks

_Sources: Khopkar ch.7 (Table 7.2, regimens for atypical mycobacterial infections); Wolverton 4e ch.9. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
